rationale: Both solutions implement the same mutex-guarded counters with the same Read, Write and count methods. They differ in how they build the combined read-write counter. A embeds readCounter and writeCounter by value and builds them with plain struct literals. That is simple and direct, and it gives one allocation with no indirection. B embeds pointers and builds them by calling the public constructors and then type-asserting the interface results back to concrete types (`.(*readCounter)`). That round trip is needlessly roundabout and would panic at runtime if a constructor were ever changed. A also adds short doc comments for each type. Its only blemish is field and key alignment that gofmt would normalise, which is cosmetic. Overall A is slightly cleaner and more direct.
